items.prompt: In a identity directory system, an account service must change a user credential. a revoked credential must not remain usable through an old session The design review focuses on audit trails, privacy obligations, and non-repudiation boundaries. The normal path is healthy and the design must show where the decision belongs. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: a revoked credential must not remain usable through an old session
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is record security-relevant actions with attributable identity, integrity, retention, and access controls..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Record security-relevant actions with attributable identity, integrity, retention, and access controls. In this normal path for identity directory, an audit trail is useful only when its writer, mutation boundary, and retention obligation are explicit. The owner must also make revocation propagation lag observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide audit trails, privacy obligations, and non-repudiation boundaries independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat revocation propagation lag as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Record security-relevant actions with attributable identity, integrity, retention, and access controls. It addresses a revoked credential must not remain usable through an old session through an explicit mechanism and keeps revocation propagation lag inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: An audit trail is useful only when its writer, mutation boundary, and retention obligation are explicit. The applicability case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For identity directory, the decision keeps a revoked credential must not remain usable through an old session attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats revocation propagation lag as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Audit trails, privacy obligations, and non-repudiation boundaries” to terminology recall. Authentication is not authorization, encryption is not isolation, and client-side controls are not enforcement; define explicit trust boundaries. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce audit trails, privacy obligations, and non-repudiation boundaries must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to Building Secure and Reliable Systems (https://google.github.io/building-secure-and-reliable-systems/raw/toc.html); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.
